newsitem.title: GERMANY: TOEPFER MAINTAINS GERMAN 1997 GRAIN CROP FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: TOEPFER MAINTAINS GERMAN 1997 GRAIN CROP FORECAST.

text.p: German grain trader Alfred C Toepfer has not revised its earlier forecasts for a 43 million tonne German grain harvest this year, it said in response to an inquiry.
Rainfall in July had lodged barley, where the harvest will be mostly finished this week, and this could cause slight volume reductions, Toepfer said.

But the barley harvest has so far brought better qualities than expected and the overall outlook for cereals from a four percent higher area remains positive, especially if the better weather pattern continues.
Wheat was looking in good shape ahead of harvesting, which will start in less than a fortnight, and maize had benefited from good warmth and moisture supply of late.
It was too early to comment on the likely rapeseed crop because of weather-induced disruptions to farmers' harvesting efforts.

But early yields looked above those seen last year and this year should bring a normal crop again -- Germany lost a third of its crop last year from damage caused by the extremely severe 1995-96 winter.
Oder river flooding over the last three weeks, although devastating thousands of hectares of farmland, was too localised to damage main growing regions of grains and oilseeds.

Even if main dikes along the German-Polish border had burst, the maximum grain area which could have been flooded, totalled just 30,000-40,000 hectares, out of Germany's more than seven million ha total.
Emergency services and soldiers last looked set to win the battle against the floods, as water levels were receding.
Farmers' organisations in the flood-hit state of Brandenburg were preparing for the massive clear-up attempt.

They were also organising practical and financial support for the 30 or so farms which have not only lost this year's crop, but will probably be unable to plant winter grain on soaked fields in the autumn.
